title: Angles of Elevation and Depression
seo_title: Elevation and Depression – SSS 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Solve problems on angles of elevation and depression using trigonometric ratios. (summary of the NERDC SSS 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 1 maths worksheets on angles of elevation and depression: heights of buildings and trees, distances and two-angle problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Elevation looks up; depression looks down.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Draw a sketch with the horizontal line and the right angle.
  • The angle of depression from the top equals the angle of elevation from the bottom (alternate angles).
  • Then use tan, sin or cos in the right-angled triangle.

Examples

Example

From 30 m away, a tree top is at 45°

h = 30 × tan 45°

Answer: 30 m

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Measuring from the verticalBoth angles are from the horizontal.
Using the wrong triangleMark the right angle at the foot.
Forgetting the observer’s heightAdd it if the question gives it.

faq.q: Are the angles of elevation and depression equal?
faq.a: Yes, between the same two points.
tan, because height and distance are opposite and adjacent.
A tool that measures angles of elevation.

items.q: Fatima stands 72 m from the foot of a tower. The angle of elevation of the top is 43° and her eyes are 1.5 m above the ground. Find the height of the tower, correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: tan 43° = height ÷ 72, so height = 72 tan 43° = 67.1 m, plus 1.5 m for the eye level. 68.6 m.
